summary_paragraph: A 60-year-old woman with a history of coronary artery disease, diabetes, and asthma was admitted for worsening cough, shortness of breath, and chest pain. She had been treated with an outpatient antibiotic starting with 'A' without improvement. Imaging revealed patchy opacity in the right upper lung consistent with pneumonia. She was started on levofloxacin and showed clinical improvement. Chest pain was present on admission but resolved and was attributed to musculoskeletal strain from coughing; cardiac workup including serial troponins and EKGs ruled out acute myocardial infarction. Influenza testing was negative, and blood cultures showed no growth. She received Pneumovax vaccination during admission. Her diabetes was managed with sliding scale insulin and home medications. She was discharged home with home services on continued antibiotics, insulin, and her baseline cardiac and chronic disease medications.
